previous_plans: 1. Set the framework: a is bounded and coercive on H1_0(Omega); F in H^{-1}(Omega). Note we will use Lax-Milgram to guarantee existence and uniqueness. 2. Existence and uniqueness for continuous problem: by Lax-Milgram there exists a unique y in H1_0(Omega) such that a(y, v) = F(v) for all v in H1_0(Omega). 3. Discrete problem setup: restrict to V_h^0 subset of H1_0(Omega); by the same boundedness and coercivity (on V_h^0) and Lax-Milgram, there exists a unique y_h in V_h^0 such that a(y_h, v_h) = F(v_h) for all v_h in V_h^0. 4. Galerkin orthogonality: subtract the discrete equation from the continuous one to obtain a(y - y_h, v_h) = 0 for all v_h in V_h^0. 5. Error identity leveraging Galerkin orthogonality: for any v_h in V_h^0, a(y - y_h, y - y_h) = a(y - y_h, y - v_h). 6. Apply boundedness and coercivity: c ||y - y_h||_1^2 ≤ |a(y - y_h, y - y_h)| ≤ C ||y - y_h||_1 ||y - v_h||_1. 7. Conclude the discrete error estimate by dividing both sides by ||y - y_h||_1 (assuming nonzero) to get ||y - y_h||_1 ≤ (C/c) ||y - v_h||_1 for all v_h in V_h^0. 8. Infimum step: take the infimum over v_h in V_h^0 to obtain ||y - y_h||_1 ≤ (C/c) inf_{v_h in V_h^0} ||y - v_h||_1. 9. Conclusion: the Cea-type error estimate holds; the bound is independent of the mesh size and depends only on the constants C and c. 10. Remark: the proof uses only Lax-Milgram and standard Galerkin orthogonality; no additional regularity assumptions are required.
